question.text: Will the Save Our Bacon Act be enacted into law before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, federal legislation is enacted into law that preempts state regulation of out-of-state pork production.

Specifically, the enacted text must establish that pork producers may raise and market their products in interstate commerce, free from state or local production-process standards imposed on pigs physically raised outside the state's borders. The statute may also cover other livestock (e.g., cattle, veal, dairy), but pork coverage is what this question turns on.
question.fine_print:
* Enactment may occur via presidential signature, becoming law without signature, or veto override. The legislation may be a standalone bill or a provision within other legislation such as the Farm Bill, appropriations, or the NDAA.
* Court rulings, executive orders, or USDA rulemakings achieving similar effects do not count.
* A bill that grandfathers existing state laws, applies only prospectively to laws enacted after a certain date, or contains a state opt-out provision will not resolve **Yes**.
* The effective date of the bill does not matter, as long as it is enacted before July 1, 2027.

research:
I found nothing that settles this yet. Two things since the House vote cut against a Yes: the Senate committee's farm bill left out the Save Our Bacon language, and Democrats are projected to win the House on November 3, 2026. So the realistic window is mainly the lame-duck session, from November 9 to about Christmas 2026. Several key pages (congress.gov and some trade press) blocked me, so I confirmed a few items only through search results.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding record is congress.gov, through enactment of H.R. 4673, H.R. 7567, or a must-pass bill that carries the same language. The H.R. 4673 page returned a 403 error, so I could not see its latest action directly. [congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/4673)
- I could not confirm whether Section 12006 of H.R. 7567 grandfathers existing state laws or applies only to future ones. Either would make it fail the resolution criteria, so this is worth checking in the bill text.

## 2. Current status
- No version has been enacted. The House bill includes the language; the Senate committee bill (S. 5526) does not. There has been no Senate floor vote and no House-Senate conference agreement.
- 2026-09-16: The Senate Agriculture Committee passed its farm bill 12-11 on party lines, without the Save Our Bacon language. Chairman Boozman blocked Sen. Ernst's amendment, saying the time for amendments had passed. Sen. Hoeven suggested she raise it on the Senate floor instead. [Iowa Capital Dispatch](https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2026/09/16/with-mcconnell-back-senate-ag-committee-advances-farm-bill-on-party-lines/), [Agri-Pulse](https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/25257-senate-ag-passes-farm-bill-along-party-lines-amid-gop-drama)
- On the Senate floor the bill needs 60 votes, and Republicans held 53 seats before the election.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: NBC, CNBC and Decision Desk HQ project that Democrats will control the House in the next Congress, which starts January 2027. Senate results were not yet clear in my searches. [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results), [NewsNation](https://www.newsnationnow.com/politics/2026-midterm-elections/house-races-to-watch-midterms-2026/)
- 2026-11-03: Competitive Markets Action, a group that defended Prop 12, dissolved, citing exhausted funds (per the news summary provided; the page returned 403). National Hog Farmer also reports a roughly $30M campaign opposing Save Our Bacon. [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farm-policy-news/pro-prop-12-group-dissolves-as-save-our-bacon-act-looms), [SAN](https://san.com/cc/the-30m-fight-over-pigs-pork-and-state-power/)
- 2026-11-02: Congress returns November 9. Farm groups say they do not want another extension. [Ottumwa Radio/Brownfield](https://ottumwaradio.com/2026/11/ag-eyeing-lame-duck-session-for-signs-of-farm-bill-life/)
- 2026-10-09: Holland & Knight says the current stopgap funding bill expires December 11 and the 2018 farm bill authorities have lapsed. It calls a full farm bill a "realistic year-end objective," with another extension as the fallback. The main sticking point is how much of SNAP costs states must share. [Holland & Knight](https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/10/beyond-the-midterms-congress-faces-converging-year-end-deadlines)
- Undated search summary: the pork producers' trade group (NPPC) reportedly sees a path to attach the fix to must-pass lame-duck legislation, such as the December 11 funding bill. I did not verify this in a primary source.
- 2026-09-06: NPPC's Kyle Garner said the farm bill is "the only vehicle available to us this year." He ruled out the defense bill (NDAA) and said a spending package would need more bipartisan support than they have. Boozman: "I don't think there's a single Democrat that would vote for it." [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/in-depth-prop-12-fight-enters-a-critical-stretch-in-congress/)
- 2026-08-06: The first committee vote to advance the bill failed 10-11 over the SNAP cost-share dispute. [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/in-depth-prop-12-fight-enters-a-critical-stretch-in-congress/)
- 2026-06 (early): Sen. Roger Marshall withdrew as a sponsor of the Senate version. On June 23, Senate Democratic Leader Schumer said he "will fight to keep it out." [Agbull](https://www.agbull.com/save-our-bacon-act-fight-intensifies-as-senate-cracks-emerge-marshall-withdrawal-reshapes-the-battle-lines/)
- 2026-06-30: Boozman said the provision lacks the Democratic votes needed on the Senate floor. [RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/boozman-explains-why-prop-12-was-left-out-of-the-senate-farm-bill)

## 4. Base rates
- This kind of provision has never become law. These are from memory, not newly sourced:
  - The King Amendment was in the 2013 House farm bill and was dropped in the final 2014 bill.
  - The Protect Interstate Commerce Act language was in the 2018 House farm bill and was dropped in the final bill.
  - The 2024 House Agriculture Committee bill included a Prop 12 fix but never reached a floor vote.
  - The EATS Act has never been enacted.
- In each of the two past cases where the House passed this language in a farm bill, it was stripped when the chambers negotiated the final bill.
- The Senate Agriculture Committee has left the language out of every draft this Congress.

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the pre-collected markets match this question:
  - The Kalshi "SAVE Act" and "SAVE America Act" markets are about an elections bill.
  - The Kalshi "Drain the Swamp Act" market and the Polymarket Florida property tax referendum are unrelated.
  - The Kalshi reconciliation market (29% by July 1, 2027) is only loosely relevant, as a possible vehicle.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or expert forecast specifically on Save Our Bacon or a Prop 12 preemption becoming law.

## 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-09: Congress returns for the lame-duck session, expected to run until about Christmas with a Thanksgiving break.
- To watch: a Senate floor vote on S. 5526, including any Ernst amendment, or the two chambers skipping a floor vote and negotiating a final bill behind closed doors. [Humane World](https://www.humaneworld.org/en/news/whats-happening-california-prop-12-farm-bill-save-our-bacon-act)
- 2026-12-11: The stopgap funding bill expires. A spending package or a farm bill extension could be used to carry the provision.
- 2027-01-03: The 120th Congress begins with a projected Democratic House, which would likely make it much harder to pass the provision through July 1, 2027. Senate control was still unclear when I searched.
- Possible budget reconciliation bill in 2027: Kalshi puts about 29% on one becoming law by July 1, 2027. Whether the Senate parliamentarian would let a preemption provision into such a bill is uncertain.

Sources: [Iowa Capital Dispatch](https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2026/09/16/with-mcconnell-back-senate-ag-committee-advances-farm-bill-on-party-lines/), [Agri-Pulse](https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/25257-senate-ag-passes-farm-bill-along-party-lines-amid-gop-drama), [Meatingplace](https://meatingplace.com/in-depth-prop-12-fight-enters-a-critical-stretch-in-congress/), [RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/boozman-explains-why-prop-12-was-left-out-of-the-senate-farm-bill), [Holland & Knight](https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/10/beyond-the-midterms-congress-faces-converging-year-end-deadlines), [Humane World](https://www.humaneworld.org/en/news/whats-happening-california-prop-12-farm-bill-save-our-bacon-act), [Ottumwa Radio](https://ottumwaradio.com/2026/11/ag-eyeing-lame-duck-session-for-signs-of-farm-bill-life/), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results), [NewsNation](https://www.newsnationnow.com/politics/2026-midterm-elections/house-races-to-watch-midterms-2026/), [Agbull](https://www.agbull.com/save-our-bacon-act-fight-intensifies-as-senate-cracks-emerge-marshall-withdrawal-reshapes-the-battle-lines/), [SAN](https://san.com/cc/the-30m-fight-over-pigs-pork-and-state-power/), [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farm-policy-news/pro-prop-12-group-dissolves-as-save-our-bacon-act-looms)

## Research brief: will the Save Our Bacon Act (Prop 12 preemption) become law before July 1, 2027?

**Bottom line:** Nothing has settled this yet. The language is in the farm bill the House passed but not in the Senate's version. Two things now weigh heavily: the November 3 midterms, where Democrats are projected to win both chambers, and the 119th Congress ending on January 3, 2027.

### 1. Resolution source
- There is no single data series to check. The question resolves on whether a statute is enacted, which would appear on Congress.gov (H.R. 4673, H.R. 7567) and as a public law.
- 2026-11-04: I could not fetch the H.R. 7567 page on Congress.gov (HTTP 403), so I can't report its latest listed action. Secondary sources show no enactment. The House passed the bill on April 30, 2026, and the Senate committee approved its own bill in September.

### 2. Current status
- Not settled. No farm bill or standalone preemption bill has been enacted.
- June 2026: Chairman Boozman's Senate draft left out the Save Our Bacon language. He said: "We're going to need a number of Democratic votes in order to get this passed on the floor." [RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/boozman-explains-why-prop-12-was-left-out-of-the-senate-farm-bill), [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/livestock-management/senate-farm-bill-draft-omits-prop-12-fix-for-pork-industry)
- 2026-09-16: The Senate Agriculture Committee approved the Agricultural Act of 2026 by 12-11 on party lines, after an earlier August markup failed. Sen. Ernst's Prop 12 amendment was blocked from a vote, and Grassley objected. Some observers say the Senate may skip a floor vote and go straight to closed-door conference talks. [KTVO](https://www.ktvo.com/news/local/senate-agriculture-committee-advances-farm-bill-as-prop-12-debate-moves-to-senate-floor/article_7fa63fb4-8d41-479d-a345-44739e3bd8ee.html), [Brownfield, 8/7](https://www.brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-outlines-path-forward-for-farm-bill-after-failed-vote/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-04: Democrats are projected to win the House (estimates range from about 239 to 255+ seats) and the Senate. Reported Senate flips include Iowa, Kansas, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, Texas and Maine. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/midterm-elections-2026-live-updates.html), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-elections/house-results), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/04/politics/live-news/midterm-election-congress)
- 2026-11-03: The pro-Prop 12 group Competitive Markets Action and its PAC shut down, citing exhausted funds. [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farm-policy-news/pro-prop-12-group-dissolves-as-save-our-bacon-act-looms) (the article blocked fetching; this is from the news summary)
- 2026-11-02 to 11-04: A RealClearInvestigations report traced the roughly $30M campaign against Save Our Bacon to Silicon Valley donors and animal-rights groups, and the National Pork Producers Council (NPPC, the main pork lobby) amplified it. Coverage says Boozman and House Chairman Thompson are both optimistic that the provision or something similar will be in a final package. It names the lame duck, starting Nov. 9, as the key window, and notes Democrats may prefer to wait until January if they win a chamber. [The Pig Site](https://www.thepigsite.com/news/2026/11/report-links-prop-12-campaign-to-tech-donors-says-nppc), [RRFN](https://www.rrfn.com/2026/11/04/report-questions-funding-behind-proposition-12-campaign/), [National Hog Farmer](https://www.nationalhogfarmer.com/farm-policy-news/prop-12-fix-fight-traced-to-silicon-valley-animal-rights-network)
- 2026-10-30: Boozman still sees a "fair chance" of a farm bill in the lame duck. He says the four committee leaders are negotiating, about 10% of the bill may need leadership (Thune and Schumer) to settle, and Trump "really wants to get a farm bill done." The Senate returns on Nov. 9. [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-farm-bill-still-has-a-chance-in-lame-duck-session/)
- Late October: Save Our Bacon/Prop 12, E15 and M-COOL (country-of-origin meat labeling) are expected to be settled in conference. SNAP state cost-sharing and error-rate rules remain the main sticking points. One analysis says a short extension is more likely than enactment by year-end. [Statt](https://statt.com/blog/from-expiration-to-agreement-whats-next-for-the-farm-bill/)
- June 2026: Sen. Roger Marshall withdrew as a sponsor of the Senate companion bill (Food Security and Farm Protection Act), calling it a drag on the farm bill. Senate Democratic Leader Schumer vowed to keep the language out. [Agri-Pulse](https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/24827-marshall-pulls-support-for-bill-to-end-californias-prop-12), [Spotlight PA](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/06/farm-bill-save-our-bacon-act-animal-welfare-state-laws-federal-government/)

### 4. Base rates
- 2013-2014: The House farm bill carried the King Amendment (Rep. Steve King's earlier version of this preemption). It was dropped in conference, and the 2014 Agricultural Act did not include it. [AWI](https://awionline.org/awi-quarterly/2013-fall/king-amendment%E2%80%99s-attack-state-animal-welfare-laws)
- 2018: The House version again included King-style preemption, and the final 2018 farm bill again left it out.
- The EATS Act was introduced in the 117th and 118th Congresses and never got a floor vote in either chamber. Federal preemption of Prop 12 has therefore never been enacted: 0 for 3 when it was in a House farm bill (2014, 2018 and, so far, 2026).
- Farm bills often run late and get extended (the 2018 law was extended in 2023 and again in 2024-2025).
- Structural point: the 119th Congress ends 2027-01-03. If there is no lame-duck deal, a Democratic-led House and Senate would hold the pen from January through the July 1, 2027 deadline.

### 5. Other forecasts
- None of the collected Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. The "SAVE Act" and "SAVE America Act" markets are about an elections bill (1-4%). The reconciliation-bill market (29% before Jul 1, 2027) and the Florida property-tax referendum are unrelated.
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on the Save Our Bacon Act or Prop 12 preemption.

### 6. Upcoming events
- 2026-11-09: The Senate returns and the lame duck begins. A farm bill conference deal, a possible Senate floor vote, or a deal folded into a December spending package or extension are all possible. [Brownfield](https://brownfieldagnews.com/news/boozman-farm-bill-still-has-a-chance-in-lame-duck-session/)
- Mid to late November: Farmers are expected to lobby Capitol Hill, and final House and Senate seat counts will come in.
- December 2026: Government funding deadlines could carry the farm bill or an extension. Watch whether any deal keeps Save Our Bacon language, narrows it, or adds grandfathering or an opt-out, which would not count.
- 2027-01-03: The new Congress begins and all pending bills must be reintroduced. Democratic chairs would control the agriculture committees.
- Other things to watch: whether Boozman's $11B farm aid package moves through the defense reconciliation bill, and any NPPC push to attach the language to must-pass bills.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left and what Yes requires.** The deadline is July 1, 2027, about 8 months away, though the realistic window is mostly the lame-duck session (November 9 to roughly late December 2026). For Yes, a statute must be enacted that preempts state production-process standards on pork raised out of state, with no grandfathering, no prospective-only limit and no state opt-out. The vehicle could be a final farm bill, a spending package, the NDAA or a standalone bill.

(b) **Status quo.** Nothing has been enacted. The Senate committee bill (S. 5526) leaves the language out, Democrats appear to have won the House for 2027, and Prop 12 stays in force. Without change, this resolves No.

(c) **Base rate.** The House has passed this language in its farm bill twice before (2013 King Amendment, 2018 Protect Interstate Commerce Act). It also appeared in the 2024 House committee bill and in every EATS Act version, and it has never been enacted. The rate is roughly 0 of 4 or 5 attempts. Using a smoothed estimate, it is about 5-10% for a cycle in which the House has passed it, before accounting for the Senate's position.

(d) **Strongest evidence.**
- **For Yes:**
  - The House passed it on April 30, 2026, and the Rules Committee blocked a vote to strip it.
  - NPPC reportedly sees a path through must-pass lame-duck legislation (unverified).
  - The main pro-Prop 12 group dissolved on November 3, 2026.
  - Republicans control the White House, and the administration is sympathetic.
- **For No:**
  - Senate Agriculture passed its bill without the language on September 16, 2026, and Boozman blocked Ernst's amendment.
  - On June 30, 2026, Boozman said the provision lacks the Democratic votes needed, and earlier he said "not a single Democrat" would vote for it.
  - Schumer vowed on June 23, 2026 to keep it out.
  - Sen. Marshall withdrew as a sponsor in June 2026.
  - On September 6, 2026, NPPC itself ruled out the NDAA and said a spending package lacks the needed bipartisan support.
  - The House is projected to flip to Democrats (November 4, 2026), closing the 2027 path.
  - A reconciliation bill would likely lose the provision to the Byrd rule, since it has no budget effect.
  - Even if a compromise emerged, it might grandfather existing laws, which would fail the criteria.

(e) **Scenarios.**
- **No:** The lame duck produces either another farm bill extension or a final farm bill that drops the provision to win 60 Senate votes, as happened in 2014 and 2018. The Democratic House kills it in 2027.
- **Yes:** In a year-end conference deal, Republican negotiators trade SNAP concessions for keeping Section 12006 in a clean form. Enough farm-state Democrats accept the package to avoid another extension, and the President signs it in December.

(f) **From base rate to final number.** I start near 7% for a House-passed cycle. I move down because:
- the Senate committee explicitly excluded the language;
- the 60-vote math is clearly unfavorable, according to the committee chairman himself;
- the trade group conceded that the alternative vehicles are not viable;
- the House flip removes the 2027 path;
- even a compromise could carry grandfather terms that fail resolution.

A little lame-duck tail risk remains, given heavy lobbying and the need for a farm bill deal. No market covers this question directly.

Probability: 3%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About eight months remain (the deadline is July 1, 2027). Yes requires a statute that preempts state production-process standards on out-of-state pork, with no grandfathering, no prospective-only limit and no state opt-out. It must be enacted through a farm bill, an appropriations bill or another vehicle. In practice, the window is the lame-duck session (November 9 to late December 2026). After January 3, 2027, a Democratic-controlled House makes enactment very unlikely.

**(b) Status quo.** Nothing is enacted. The Senate Agriculture Committee bill omits the language, so the status quo outcome is No.

**(c) Base rate.** This language has been tried repeatedly and never enacted:
- the King Amendment in 2013-14,
- the Protect Interstate Commerce Act language in 2018,
- the 2024 House Agriculture Committee bill,
- the EATS Act across several Congresses.

In both cases where the House passed it in a farm bill, conferees stripped it. That puts the base rate near 0 of 4. A reasonable prior for any single cycle is about 5-10%, and lower once the Senate has already excluded it.

**(d) Evidence.**

*For Yes:*
- The House passed the language in its farm bill on April 30, 2026, 224-200.
- NPPC reportedly sees a lame-duck path through must-pass legislation (unverified).
- A pro-Prop 12 group dissolved on November 3, 2026.
- Farm groups want a full farm bill this year rather than another extension.

*For No:*
- The Senate committee bill (September 16, 2026) excluded the language, and Boozman blocked the Ernst amendment.
- Boozman said on June 30 that it lacks the Democratic votes for 60, and later said "I don't think there's a single Democrat that would vote for it."
- Schumer vowed on June 23 to fight it.
- Sen. Marshall withdrew as a sponsor in early June.
- NPPC said on September 6 that the NDAA is ruled out and a spending package lacks bipartisan support.
- The farm bill itself is stalled over SNAP cost-sharing, with an extension as the fallback.
- Democrats are projected on November 4 to win the House for 2027.

**(e) Scenarios.**

*No:* The lame duck passes a continuing resolution and a farm bill extension, or a slimmed final farm bill without the Prop 12 language because Senate Democrats demand its removal to reach 60 votes. The Democratic House in 2027 blocks any further attempt. This is very likely.

*Yes:* Leaders negotiate a final farm bill informally, skipping a Senate floor vote. Republicans trade SNAP concessions to farm-state Democrats in exchange for keeping a non-grandfathered Prop 12 fix. The bill clears 60 votes in December and is signed. A 2027 reconciliation bill carrying it is a remote alternative, because Byrd rule problems make it unlikely.

**(f) Adjustment.** I start from a cycle base rate of about 7%. I move down because the Senate committee already excluded the language and leading Democrats are openly opposed. I also move down because the post-election House flip removes most of the 2027 window. There is a small additional risk that the House text grandfathers existing laws and would fail the criteria anyway. A small residual remains for a lame-duck deal. No matching market exists to anchor on.

Probability: 3%

**(a) Time left and what Yes requires.** About 8 months remain, to July 1, 2027. The practical window is shorter: mainly the lame-duck session, from November 9 to about late December 2026.

For Yes, a law must be enacted that preempts state production-process standards on pork raised out of state. It cannot grandfather existing laws, apply only to future laws, or let states opt out. The likely vehicles are:
- a final farm bill (a conference version of H.R. 7567 and S. 5526),
- the December 11 government funding bill or a farm bill extension, or
- in 2027, a reconciliation bill or a bill passed by a Democratic House, which is very unlikely.

**(b) Status quo.** Nothing has been enacted. The Senate committee bill leaves the language out, and no final bill has been negotiated. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

**(c) Base rate.** The House has passed King Amendment-type language in its farm bill twice, in 2013 and 2018. Both times it was dropped from the final bill, so 0 of 2 became law, and the EATS Act has never been enacted. More broadly, contested House-only riders that lack Senate support and face 60-vote opposition rarely survive negotiations with the Senate, perhaps 5-10% of the time. I use a base rate of about 5%.

**(d) Evidence.**
For Yes:
- The House passed the farm bill with the language on April 30, 2026, and the Rules Committee blocked the amendment to strip it.
- Sen. Ernst plans to push it on the Senate floor.
- The NPPC reportedly sees a path through must-pass lame-duck legislation.
- The leading pro-Prop 12 advocacy group dissolved on November 3, 2026.
- Farm groups want a full farm bill rather than another extension.

For No:
- The Senate committee passed its bill 12-11 on September 16, 2026, without the language.
- Boozman said on June 30 that the provision lacks Democratic votes, and said on September 6 that no single Democrat would vote for it.
- Schumer pledged on June 23 to fight to keep it out.
- Sen. Marshall withdrew as a sponsor of the Senate version.
- On September 6, NPPC ruled out the defense bill and conceded that a spending bill would need bipartisan support it does not have.
- Democrats were projected on November 4 to win the House for 2027, which effectively closes the post-January window.
- The SNAP cost-share dispute may push the whole farm bill to another extension.

**(e) Scenarios.**
- No: The lame duck produces a stopgap funding bill and a farm bill extension, and the provision is dropped. Alternatively, a slimmed-down bipartisan farm bill passes without it, as Senate Democrats demand. The Democratic House in 2027 then refuses to take it up.
- Yes: House Republicans insist in final negotiations, a few farm-state Democrats accept a compromise version to get a farm bill done before losing leverage, and the final bill clears the Senate with 60 votes. The compromise text must also avoid grandfathering, which is itself a risk because compromises often grandfather existing laws.
